explanation: `git log` provides the complete history chain.
tip: Add `-p` to see the actual code diff inside the log: `git log -p`.

explanation: `--oneline` is the fastest way to get an overview of recent work.
tip: Combine flags: `git log --oneline -n 5` shows only the last 5 commits.

explanation: Press `q` to quit the pager. Spacebar scrolls down, `b` scrolls up.
tip: You can also search inside git log by typing `/keyword` and pressing Enter.

explanation: `git diff` without flags inspects changes that haven't been staged yet.
tip: Run `git diff` before `git add` to review your own work before staging.

explanation: `--staged` and `--cached` are exact synonyms in Git.
tip: Use this right before committing to be 100% sure what will be in the snapshot.

explanation: Green `+` lines are additions; red `-` lines are deletions.
tip: Modifying a line shows up as deleting the old line and adding the new line.

explanation: You only need the first 7 characters of a hash to identify a commit uniquely in most commands.
`HEAD` points to the branch or commit you are currently checked out on.
tip: `HEAD~1` refers to the commit immediately before HEAD.

explanation: `git show` inspects any Git object (commit, tag, tree).
tip: `git show <hash>` lets you inspect any past commit at any time.

explanation: Follow Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`) for crystal-clear team logs.
tip: Keep the first line under 50-72 characters.
